title: Dollar Industries Ltd - 541403 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Dollar Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13.2% YoY to INR622 crore, but gross margin fell 169 bps to 28.1% on mix and cotton costs; price hikes of 4-6% planned.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 operating income grew 13.2% YoY to INR622 crore and volume grew 12.0%, but gross margin compressed 169 bps to 28.1% as the economy segment rose to 47% of revenue and cotton/yarn costs rose. Operating EBITDA grew only 2.0% to INR58 crore (9.3% margin), while PAT rose 11.4% to INR33 crore. For FY26, operating income rose 10.0% to INR1,881 crore, EBITDA 9.3% to INR200 crore (10.6% margin) and PAT 18.0% to INR107 crore. Management implemented a calibrated price hike in April (3-4%) and plans another 2-3% in June, and it deferred FY27 guidance to the Q1 call.

segments.name: Economy (Dollar Always)
segments.commentary: Rose to 47% of Q4 revenue from 45% in Q4 FY25 and about 41% for FY26 (FY25: 39.1%); management cited this as the main driver of lower realisation.

segments.name: Dollar Man / Regular and Big Boss
segments.commentary: Regular 41.5% and Big Boss 36.5% of FY26 revenue; Dollar Man category share fell to 36.5% from 38.8% in FY25.

segments.name: Missy (women's)
segments.commentary: About 7.5% of FY26 revenue, down from 8.0% in FY25.

segments.name: Thermals
segments.commentary: 6.1% of FY26 revenue, up from 5.9% in FY25.

segments.name: Force NXT (super premium)
segments.commentary: Value +16.5% and volume +26.2% in FY26; 4.5% of revenue, up from 4.2%. Q4 value +16.0%, volume +24.3%.

segments.name: Dollar Protect (rainwear)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume +49.9%; FY26 volume +18%; 2.1% of revenue.

segments.name: Quick commerce / non-traditional channels
segments.commentary: Quick commerce grew 437% YoY and rose to 2.5% of revenue from 0.5%; non-traditional channels (MT, e-commerce, QC) grew 24.2% in FY26.

segments.name: G.O.A.T alliance
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR49 crore (+45% YoY), PAT INR4.9 crore (~10% margin).

segments.name: Pepe Inner Fashion JV
segments.commentary: Only bottom line consolidated (51% stake); revenue not in top line; D2C via large-format stores.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 guidance; management will give full-year guidance on or before the Q1 FY27 call.
Management expects double-digit volume and value growth in FY27 and says margins should be better than FY26 (FY26 EBITDA margin 10.6%; management cited ~10.82%).
Price hikes: about 3-4% in April and 2-3% in June (total 4-6%; CFO cited 6-7%); management says no further hike is needed as cotton and yarn prices stabilise.
Cash conversion cycle to fall a further 5-7 days in FY27, mainly from receivable days.
Modern trade expected to grow 20-25% in FY27.
Debt of about INR264 crore expected to be reduced to zero by FY28; no major capex planned.
capex_capacity: No major capex commitments in the near term; capacity can be flexed 20-30% by adding job workers without capex.
FY26 production volume about 28 crore pieces; knitting, bleaching and cutting are in-house, while stitching (mainly economy and mix) is outsourced to job workers.
Pilot run of Phase 2 of Project Lakshya has started, focused on deepening active retailers in gold states; non-dominant state entry is on hold pending tailored strategies.
Merger of nine promoter (RPT) companies: NCLT application filed and first motion approved; expected to save INR4-5 crore a year in royalty, service charges and rent, with negligible revenue effect.
demand_pricing: Q4 gross margin decline attributed mainly to economy-segment mix (47%) and higher yarn prices that were not passed on; management denied meaningful down-trading and said the shift was temporary.
Demand described as stable; Q4 retail footfall dipped due to heat, which management called timing, not structural.
Management says the price hike has not hurt demand and that competitive intensity is stabilising; no market share loss is expected since peers are also raising prices.
Lakshya contribution to revenue was about 27% in Q4 versus 29% a year earlier, but management said the full-year contribution was flat.

qa_highlights.question: Is the price hike a one-off, how large is it, and does it come with scheme rollbacks?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry-wide hike after about 2 years: 3-4% in April and 2-3% in June, total about 4-6% (CFO cited 6-7%). It is a pure price increase; schemes and discounts are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Can debt of INR264 crore be substantially reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said debt can be reduced to zero by FY28; about INR50 crore of short- and long-term borrowings were repaid last year. Management expects further cash from a 5-7 day cycle reduction.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 gross margin decline, cotton or competition?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said mix (economy at 47%) and yarn costs were the main factors; prices were unchanged while realisation fell. Management denied meaningful discounting.

qa_highlights.question: Is the economy-segment shift structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is temporary, citing high demand in Tier 2/3 and rural areas, formalisation from unorganised players, and advertising of Dollar Lehar from the past three years. Force NXT grew 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin return to double digits and what is the FY27 growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 margins should be better than FY26 and it is eyeing double-digit growth, but gave no specific number and deferred guidance to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory and working-capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days fell from about 130 to 100; management said optimised inventory is 95-100 days given the 90-day production cycle, and receivables are the main lever for the next 5-7 day reduction.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure: Q4 gross margin fell 169 bps; whether June price hike offsets yarn costs and mix is the key Q1 test.
Economy-segment share at 47% of revenue; a continued shift would keep realisation and margin pressured.
Q1 demand softness from heat and footfall; management says it is timing, not structural.
Lakshya Phase 2 pilot results and the pace of new-state entry, which management has put on hold.
Working capital: receivable-day reduction of 5-7 days is targeted; inventory days may not stay at FY26 levels.
Merger of promoter companies (NCLT) and the JV's contribution to consolidated bottom line.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and margin recovery, and on debt reduction, but evasive on FY27 numbers: guidance was deferred to Q1, and the growth percentage was not given when pressed. Audio issues interrupted the call several times.
key_quotes: Our net cash from operating activities as a proportion of Operating EBITDA stood at 70% as of 31st March 2026, affirming that our reported profits are backed by real cash generation.
So the price hike that we have taken in the Q1, I think we don't have to take any further price hike now.
It's not a structural thing which is happening. It's a very temporary thing.
Right now, I'm unable to give you a number and we will surely come back with a number on or before the Q1 earnings call.

growth.why: Management is eyeing double-digit revenue and volume/value growth for FY27 with margins better than FY26 and modern trade up 20-25%, but the formal number is deferred to the Q1 call and the backing is price hikes (4-6%), demand stability and a flexible job-worker model with no major capex, so support is vague.
